source.subject: perf(judge): eliminate ceil(N/4) batch latency via /submissions/batch API

bugs.title: perf(judge): eliminate ceil(N/4) batch latency via /submissions/batch API
bugs.root_cause:
Root cause of ~22.9s Codebox wall-time for 13 TCs was confirmed:

  Problem 1 — Sequential batching overhead:
    gather_with_concurrency(4) created ceil(13/4)=4 effective waves.
    Each wave blocked until all 4 TCs finished (~7s each).
    Result: 4 × 5.75s ≈ 22.9s total.

  Problem 2 — wait=true not honored:
    Codebox returned status_id<3 + token on every submission,
    forcing the per-TC polling loop (0.3s × ~23 polls = 6.9s/TC).

Fixes:
  1. Batch API path (CodeboxProvider._execute_batch_api):
     - POST /submissions/batch with all N TCs in one request
     - Single polling loop covers all N TCs (GET /submissions/batch?tokens=...)
     - Codebox handles internal parallelism with its own worker pool
     - Expected: wall time collapses from ceil(N/4)×7s → max(TC_wall)≈7s (3× speedup)
     - Auto-fallback: ValueError (malformed response) or HTTP 404 → per-TC path

  2. Exponential-backoff polling (both batch and per-TC paths):
     - Starts at 50ms (CODEBOX_POLL_INITIAL_SECONDS, default 0.05)
     - Backs off × 1.5 per poll up to CODEBOX_POLL_SECONDS (default 0.3s)
     - Catches sub-second completions faster without hammering server

  3. Stage-level DEBUG logging:
     - [Codebox|batch]: submit_ms, poll_count, resolved/total, final_interval_ms
     - [Codebox|tc]: wait=true status, token, poll_count, elapsed_ms

Config knobs added to .env (all optional, sane defaults):
  CODEBOX_USE_BATCH_API=true          # set false to force per-TC
  CODEBOX_POLL_INITIAL_SECONDS=0.05   # first poll delay

Tests: 16/16 passing (added test_provider_turnaround_via_batch_api)

source.author: santusht06
source.subject: fix(db): add expire_on_rollback=False to AsyncSessionLocal

bugs.title: fix(db): add expire_on_rollback=False to AsyncSessionLocal
bugs.root_cause:
Root cause of the greenlet_spawn error:
  await db.rollback() is called in assessment_service and
  contest_execution_service before long-running sandbox/Docker
  execution to release the PostgreSQL connection back to the pool.
  SQLAlchemy's default behaviour is to expire ALL loaded ORM objects
  on rollback — identical to what happens after commit.

  When the code after sandbox execution tries to access any attribute
  on those expired objects (session.id, problem.title, contest.starts_at,
  etc.), SQLAlchemy fires a lazy-load to refresh from DB.
  Lazy loads are synchronous IO; they cannot be awaited inside the
  async greenlet that SQLAlchemy async uses internally.
  Result: 'greenlet_spawn has not been called; can't call await_only()'

Fix:
  expire_on_rollback=False tells SQLAlchemy not to expire objects on
  rollback.  This is the standard solution for async SQLAlchemy apps
  that release connections mid-request.  All ORM objects retain their
  in-memory state after the rollback, so subsequent attribute access
  is served from the Python-side cache with zero DB round-trips.

source.subject: perf(navigation): lift prefetch to global delegated listener — covers all links

bugs.title: perf(navigation): lift prefetch to global delegated listener — covers all links
bugs.root_cause:
Replace per-link onMouseEnter/onTouchStart wiring with a single
document-level delegated listener mounted once in AppRoutes via
usePrefetchOnIntent hook.

How it works:
- document.addEventListener('mouseover', ...) with { passive: true }
  catches hover over any <a> in the entire DOM via event bubbling.
  mouseover fires once per element entry (not on every pixel move).
- Parses the href to determine route type (static route, contest
  overview/lobby/results, or profile) and calls the right prefetcher.
- 1-second debounce per href prevents redundant refires on same link.
- swrFetch in-flight deduplication ensures at most one request per key
  regardless of how many times the listener fires.
- Zero per-component boilerplate needed — works automatically for any
  future link added anywhere in the app.

Revert manual onMouseEnter/onTouchStart from:
  ContestsHubPage (3 call-sites)
  LeaderboardPage (1 call-site)
  CadetProfileHoverCard (1 call-site)

New file: src/hooks/usePrefetchOnIntent.ts

bugs.title: fix(deploy): add --delete to frontend rsync to prevent stale asset accumulation
bugs.root_cause:
Previously, each deploy appended new build artifacts without removing old ones.
This caused 2418 JS files (155MB) to accumulate on the server instead of the

content-hashed chunks with new filenames, so old files were never overwritten.

Fix: add --delete so rsync makes the server exactly mirror dist/ on each deploy.

source.subject: feat: production backend hardening

bugs.title: feat: production backend hardening
bugs.root_cause:
Rate Limiting (Redis sliding window):
- New middleware/rate_limit.py — sliding-window rate limiter via Redis
  pipeline (ZREMRANGEBYSCORE + ZCARD + ZADD + EXPIRE).
  Fails open when Redis is unavailable (no false positives).
- /run endpoint: 30 req/60s per user (sample-test spam protection)
- /submit endpoint: 5 req/60s per user (judge queue protection)

Background Tasks (production async workers):
- New services/background_tasks_service.py with two coroutines:
  1. session_expiry_loop (60s interval): auto-submits in-progress
     AssessmentSessions whose 120-min clock has expired. Without this,
     a session is only closed on the user's next request.
  2. auto_qualify_loop (120s interval): after the assessment window
     closes marks the Top-30 AssessmentSessions as is_top_30_qualified,
     so the live contest gate works without organiser intervention.
- Both tasks are idempotent and cancel cleanly on lifespan shutdown.

Lifespan update (main.py):
- Spawns background tasks at startup and cancels them on shutdown.
- /api/health now reports redis + judge_provider status in body.
